Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 51, verse 1–19:

Meccan, and it has one thousand two hundred and eighty-seven letters, three hundred and sixty words, and sixty verses.

Nafil ibn Raqim ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Naji informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn al-Yasa' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abdullah al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Khunays, from Ubayy, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah 'al-Dhariyat' will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every wind that blew and moved in the world" [94] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/252.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿By the winnowing winds, scattering (dhara'an)﴾: the winds that scatter dust, scattering it. It is said: the wind scattered the dust and dispersed it.

Ibn Fanjuwayh informed us, saying: Ibn Majah narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Sayyar ibn Hatim narrated to us, saying: Ayyub ibn Khawt narrated to us, saying: Umar al-A'raj narrated to us, saying: It has reached us that the dwelling places of the winds are beneath the wings of the Karubiyyun, the bearers of the Kursi. From there they stir and fall upon the wheel of the sun; then they stir from the wheel of the sun and fall upon the mountaintops; then they stir from the mountaintops and fall upon the land. As for the north wind (al-Shamal), it passes by the Garden of Eden, takes from the sweat of its fragrance, and passes over the spirits of the truthful. Then it takes its portion from the Kursi of the Great Bear (Banat Na'sh) to the west of the sun. The south-west wind (al-Dabur) comes with its portion from the west of the sun to the rising of Suhayl (Canopus). The south wind (al-Janub) comes with its portion from the rising of Suhayl to the rising of the sun. The east wind (al-Saba) comes with its portion from the rising of the sun to the Kursi of the Great Bear. So these do not enter the limit of those, nor those the limit of these.

Al-Hasan informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn ibn Dayzil narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam [in the manuscript: "al," and the apparent reading is what we have established] Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding ﴿By the winnowing winds, scattering﴾, that he said: "the winds."

﴿And those that carry the burden of rain (waqran)﴾: he said: "the clouds." ﴿And those that run with ease (yusran)﴾: he said: "the ships."

﴿And those that distribute the command (amran)﴾: he said: "the angels."

﴿Indeed, what you are promised (of good and evil, reward and punishment) is true﴾, and ﴿indeed, the Judgment (al-din: the reckoning and recompense) is surely to occur﴾, meaning: certain, bound to come to pass.

Then he began another oath, saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿By the sky having the paths (al-hubuk)﴾. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and al-Rabi' said: "possessing good, well-proportioned creation." This is also the view of Ikrimah, who said: "Have you not seen the weaver when he weaves a garment and perfects its weaving? It is said: how fine is its hubk (weaving)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "adorned with ornament." Al-Hasan said: "the stars were woven (hubikat al-nujum)."

Mujahid said: "the one with firmly built structure." al-Dahhak said: "possessing paths," but these are far from the servants so they do not see them. He said: from it comes "hubk" of sand and water when the wind strikes them, and "hubk" of curly hair and of armour, and it is the plural of "hibak" and "hubaykah." The rajaz poet said:

As if the Hawwak had covered it: a carpet in its weaving of hibak.

And from it, the hadith concerning the description of the mountains: "firm, with hubk hubk," meaning curled.

Ibn Zayd said: "possessing strength," and he recited the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And We built above you seven firm (shidad)﴾. Abdullah ibn Amr said: "it is the seventh heaven."

﴿Indeed, you, O people of Makkah, are in a divergent word (qawlin mukhtalif)﴾ concerning the Qur'an and Muhammad (peace be upon him): so some affirm and some deny, some accept and some reject. It was also said: it was revealed concerning the al-Muqtasimun (those who divided the Qur'an).

﴿Turned away (yu'fak) from it﴾: turned away from faith in both of them. ﴿Whoever is turned away (man ufik)﴾: turned away (sarafa Fanjuwayh). It was also said: "turned away from this word," i.e., because of it and on account of it, from faith, is one who is turned away. That is because they used to meet the man who wished to believe and say to him: "He is a sorcerer, a soothsayer, and a madman," turning him away from faith. This is the meaning of Mujahid's statement.

"'An" may also mean "ajl" (because of). al-Absi recited:

Because of a she-camel of ancient stock, whose owner wished to buy her from him, as if the colour of salt were upon her blades.

That is, because of a she-camel of ancient stock.

﴿Killed be the fabricators (al-kharrasun)﴾: the liars.

Ibn Abbas said: "the doubters," and they are the al-Muqtasimun who divided Allah's punishment and divided their speech about the Prophet (ﷺ) in order to turn people away from the religion of Islam.

Mujahid said: "the soothsayers."

﴿Who are in heedlessness (ghamrah)﴾: doubt and negligence. ﴿Inattentive (sahun)﴾: heedless.

﴿They ask: when is the Day of Judgment?﴾: when is the Day of Resurrection, mocking and denying.

Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿On the Day they will be tormented over the Fire (yawma hum ala al-nari yuftanun)﴾: that is, this recompense will be on a day when they are tormented, burned, and roasted by fire, just as gold is tested by fire. Its figurative sense here with the word "ʿalā" ("over") is that they are made to stand over the Fire. It was also said: it carries the meaning of "bi" (by).

And the keepers will say to them: ﴿Taste your trial (fitnatakum) this﴾; he did not say "this" in the feminine because "fitnah" here means punishment, so the reference of the demonstrative returns to the meaning: "that which you used to seek to hasten."

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them (ma atahum rabbuhum)﴾: of reward and kinds of honour.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means taking what their Lord commanded them, acting upon the obligations He imposed on them.

﴿Indeed, they were before that (kanu qabla dhalika)﴾: before entering Paradise, doing good (muhsinin) in the world. It was also said: before the revelation of the obligations, they were doing good in their deeds.

﴿They used to sleep but little of the night (kanu qalilan mina al-layli ma yahja'un)﴾: the scholars differed over the status of "ma." Some made it a negation, and said: the sentence is complete at His words "kanu qalilan," meaning they were few among people; then he began "ma yahja'un," meaning they did not sleep at night, but stood in prayer and worship. Others made it mean "alladhi" (who), and the sentence is connected, its meaning being: they were a little of the night, the sleep of which they slept, because when a verb is connected to "ma" it takes the sense of a verbal noun, as in His words: "bima zalamu" (by their wrongdoing). Others made it a connecting particle, meaning: they were few of the night who slept.

Muhammad ibn Ali said: "They did not sleep until they had prayed the 'atamah (night prayer)."

Anas ibn Malik said: they prayed between Maghrib and 'Isha'. Mutarrif said: there was rarely a night that came upon them in which they did not pray to Allah, glorified is He, either at its beginning or in its middle. al-Hasan said: they slept only the least part of the night, and sometimes they were energetic and extended their worship until the pre-dawn.

﴿And in the hours before dawn they seek forgiveness﴾. ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar (sa'il) and the deprived (mahrum)﴾: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: the beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the destitute (mihraf) who has no share in Islam.

Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: the beggar is the one who asks you, and the deprived is the one who abstains and does not ask you. Ibrahim said: it is the one who has no share in the spoils of war. This is supported by what Sufyan narrated from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a expedition, and they gained spoils; then some people who had not witnessed the spoils came, and this verse was revealed.

Ikrimah said: the deprived is the one whose wealth does not grow. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the one afflicted in his fruit, his crop, or the offspring of his livestock.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Farisi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: the deprived is the one in need. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, we are burdened with debt, rather we are deprived (mahrumun)﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: verse 67.]], and its parallel in the story of the people of Dhurwan [[Dhurwan: the name of a land in Yemen where the garden referred to is located. See al-Durr al-Manthur 6:253.]]: ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾ [[Surah al-Qalam: 27.]]. And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, saying: Abd [... ] [[Blank space in the original.]] narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Asim—meaning al-Ahwal—from Abu Qilabah, who said: a man from the people of al-Yamamah had wealth, then a flood came and took his wealth, and a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is the deprived, so give to him."

Al-Sha'bi said: I was perplexed about knowing who the deprived is; I have asked about the deprived for seventy years, and today I am no more knowledgeable than I was on that day.

Its root in the language is "the prevented," from deprivation (hirman), which is prevention.

Abu Suhayl ibn Habib informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Uthman al-Nufayli al-Harrani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abbas al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Umarah ibn Safwan al-Kala'i narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man—the son of the sister of Sa'id ibn Jubayr—who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "O Anas, woe to the rich from the poor on the Day of Resurrection; they will say: 'O Lord, they wronged us in our rights which You imposed upon them.' He will say: 'By My might and My majesty, I will bring you near and I will keep them far.'" [95] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/114.]]

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then recited to them this verse: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

As if the Hawwak had covered it: a carpet in its weaving of hibak.

And from it, the hadith concerning the description of the mountains: "firm, with hubk hubk," meaning curled.

Ibn Zayd said: "possessing strength," and he recited the words of Allah, glorified is He: ﴿And We built above you seven firm (shidad)﴾. Abdullah ibn Amr said: "it is the seventh heaven."

Ibn Abbas said: "the doubters," and they are the al-Muqtasimun who divided Allah's punishment and divided their speech about the Prophet (ﷺ) in order to turn people away from the religion of Islam.

Mujahid said: "the soothsayers."

﴿Who are in heedlessness (ghamrah)﴾: doubt and negligence. ﴿Inattentive (sahun)﴾: heedless.

﴿Turned away (yu'fak) from it﴾: turned away from faith in both of them. ﴿Whoever is turned away (man ufik)﴾: turned away (sarafa Fanjuwayh). It was also said: "turned away from this word," i.e., because of it and on account of it, from faith, is one who is turned away. That is because they used to meet the man who wished to believe and say to him: "He is a sorcerer, a soothsayer, and a madman," turning him away from faith. This is the meaning of Mujahid's statement.

"'An" may also mean "ajl" (because of). al-Absi recited:

Because of a she-camel of ancient stock, whose owner wished to buy her from him, as if the colour of salt were upon her blades.

That is, because of a she-camel of ancient stock.

﴿Killed be the fabricators (al-kharrasun)﴾: the liars.

Ibn Abbas said: "the doubters," and they are the al-Muqtasimun who divided Allah's punishment and divided their speech about the Prophet (ﷺ) in order to turn people away from the religion of Islam.

Mujahid said: "the soothsayers."

﴿Who are in heedlessness (ghamrah)﴾: doubt and negligence. ﴿Inattentive (sahun)﴾: heedless.

﴿They ask: when is the Day of Judgment?﴾: when is the Day of Resurrection, mocking and denying.

Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿On the Day they will be tormented over the Fire (yawma hum ala al-nari yuftanun)﴾: that is, this recompense will be on a day when they are tormented, burned, and roasted by fire, just as gold is tested by fire. Its figurative sense here with the word "ʿalā" ("over") is that they are made to stand over the Fire. It was also said: it carries the meaning of "bi" (by).

And the keepers will say to them: ﴿Taste your trial (fitnatakum) this﴾; he did not say "this" in the feminine because "fitnah" here means punishment, so the reference of the demonstrative returns to the meaning: "that which you used to seek to hasten."

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them (ma atahum rabbuhum)﴾: of reward and kinds of honour.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means taking what their Lord commanded them, acting upon the obligations He imposed on them.

﴿Indeed, they were before that (kanu qabla dhalika)﴾: before entering Paradise, doing good (muhsinin) in the world. It was also said: before the revelation of the obligations, they were doing good in their deeds.

﴿They used to sleep but little of the night (kanu qalilan mina al-layli ma yahja'un)﴾: the scholars differed over the status of "ma." Some made it a negation, and said: the sentence is complete at His words "kanu qalilan," meaning they were few among people; then he began "ma yahja'un," meaning they did not sleep at night, but stood in prayer and worship. Others made it mean "alladhi" (who), and the sentence is connected, its meaning being: they were a little of the night, the sleep of which they slept, because when a verb is connected to "ma" it takes the sense of a verbal noun, as in His words: "bima zalamu" (by their wrongdoing). Others made it a connecting particle, meaning: they were few of the night who slept.

Muhammad ibn Ali said: "They did not sleep until they had prayed the 'atamah (night prayer)."

Anas ibn Malik said: they prayed between Maghrib and 'Isha'. Mutarrif said: there was rarely a night that came upon them in which they did not pray to Allah, glorified is He, either at its beginning or in its middle. al-Hasan said: they slept only the least part of the night, and sometimes they were energetic and extended their worship until the pre-dawn.

﴿And in the hours before dawn they seek forgiveness﴾. ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar (sa'il) and the deprived (mahrum)﴾: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: the beggar is the one who asks people, and the deprived is the destitute (mihraf) who has no share in Islam.

Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: the beggar is the one who asks you, and the deprived is the one who abstains and does not ask you. Ibrahim said: it is the one who has no share in the spoils of war. This is supported by what Sufyan narrated from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a expedition, and they gained spoils; then some people who had not witnessed the spoils came, and this verse was revealed.

Ikrimah said: the deprived is the one whose wealth does not grow. Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the one afflicted in his fruit, his crop, or the offspring of his livestock.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Farisi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Naqid narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: the deprived is the one in need. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, we are burdened with debt, rather we are deprived (mahrumun)﴾ [[Surah al-Waqi'ah: verse 67.]], and its parallel in the story of the people of Dhurwan [[Dhurwan: the name of a land in Yemen where the garden referred to is located. See al-Durr al-Manthur 6:253.]]: ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾ [[Surah al-Qalam: 27.]]. And al-Husayn informed us, saying: Umar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, saying: Abd [... ] [[Blank space in the original.]] narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Asim—meaning al-Ahwal—from Abu Qilabah, who said: a man from the people of al-Yamamah had wealth, then a flood came and took his wealth, and a man from the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is the deprived, so give to him."

Al-Sha'bi said: I was perplexed about knowing who the deprived is; I have asked about the deprived for seventy years, and today I am no more knowledgeable than I was on that day.

Its root in the language is "the prevented," from deprivation (hirman), which is prevention.

Abu Suhayl ibn Habib informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa informed us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Uthman al-Nufayli al-Harrani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Abbas al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Umarah ibn Safwan al-Kala'i narrated to us, from al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man—the son of the sister of Sa'id ibn Jubayr—who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "O Anas, woe to the rich from the poor on the Day of Resurrection; they will say: 'O Lord, they wronged us in our rights which You imposed upon them.' He will say: 'By My might and My majesty, I will bring you near and I will keep them far.'" [95] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/114.]]

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then recited to them this verse: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾.

﴿And in the earth are signs for those who are certain.﴾

﴿And in yourselves too. Will you not see?﴾

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Tayyib al-Kalabadhi informed us, by my reading to him, saying:

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, saying: al-Sari ibn Khuzaymah al-Abiwardi narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi', from al-Zubayr, regarding ﴿And in yourselves, will you not see?﴾, that he said: "It is the path of the excrement and the urine." Al-Musayyab ibn Shurayk said: "[A person] eats and drinks from one place, and excretes from two places. Even if he drinks pure milk, it comes out as water. That is the sign in the self."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: ﴿And in yourselves, will you not see?﴾ means: in the transformation of conditions, the weakening of strength, the subjugation of [one's] power, the inability of the joints, the dissolving of resolve and the breaking of determination. Then the Exalted and Glorified informed that He placed your provision where the weevil cannot eat it and thieves cannot reach it, so He said: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised.﴾ That means the rain and the snow, by which the earth brings forth vegetation, which is the cause of sustenance. Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is: "And in the rain and the vegetation is the cause of your provision." So the rain was called "sky" (sama') because it descends from the sky. The poet said:

"When the sky falls upon a people's land,
we graze upon it, even if they are angry."

Ibn Kaysan said: it means "and upon the Lord of the heaven is your provision," with fi (in) meaning 'ala (upon), like His saying: ﴿on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:71]. The Lord is mentioned briefly, like His saying: ﴿and ask the town﴾ [Yusuf 12:82]. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾ [Hud 11:6].

Aqil informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mu'tazz, of the people of al-Rayy, narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, who said: Wasil al-Ahdab recited this verse: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised.﴾ Then he said: "Do I not see my provision in the sky, while I seek it in the earth?" So he entered a ruin and remained there three days without obtaining anything. When it was the third day, he saw a cluster of dates (jullah min ratb). He had a brother who had a better intention than he did, so he entered with him, and the two became two clusters [of dates]. This remained their practice until death separated them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Khamis narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mujahid narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Hashim al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Bazzah narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid narrated to us, from Shibl ibn Abbad, from Ibn Abi Najih, that he read: "And in the heaven is your provider (raziqukum) and what you are promised" with an alif, meaning Allah.

Mujahid said: ﴿and what you are promised﴾ is of good or evil. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿and what you are promised﴾ is of Paradise and Hell.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Alawiyyah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab ibn Shurayk narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah said: "I heard Ibn Sirin say: ﴿and what you are promised﴾ is the Hour."

﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth, [just] like what you speak.﴾ That is, that what you have mentioned concerning the matter of provision is true. The reading "mithla" with a raised vowel (raf') was recited by the people of Kufa, as a substitute for "al-haqq" (the truth), while others read it with a fatha (nasb), meaning "like" (ka-mithl). [Grammatical analysis, i'rab, here concerns the case of the word.]

﴿what you speak﴾, so that you say: "There is no god but Allah." It was said: "Just as you are beings who speak, endowed with the rational speaking faculty, so you speak. This is true, just as it is true that the human being speaks." Some of the wise said: "Just as every person speaks with the tongue of his own self, and cannot speak with the tongue of another, so every person eats his own provision that has been allotted to him, and cannot eat the provision of another."

Al-Hasan said regarding this verse: "It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'May Allah fight against people to whom their Lord swore by Himself, yet they did not believe Him.'" [96] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/267.]

Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan al-Ka'ini, Abu al-Tayyib al-Khayyat and Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Mansur, the judge in Constantinople, informed us, saying: Abu Raja' Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas ibn al-Faraj al-Riyashi al-Basri narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Asma'i say: "I came one day from the Friday mosque in Basra, and while I was in one of its alleys, a rough, coarse Bedouin came upon me, on his riding camel, with his sword hung on him and a bow in his hand. He drew near, greeted me, and said to me: 'Who is the man?' I said: 'From the Banu al-Asma'.' He said: 'Are you al-Asma'i?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And where have you come from?' I said: 'From a place full of the speech of the Most Merciful.' He said: 'Does the Most Merciful have speech that people recite?'

I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Recite some of it to me.' I said to him: 'Get down from your camel.' So he dismounted, and I began with the sura of al-Dhariyat. When I reached His saying: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised﴾, he said: 'O Asma'i, is this the speech of the Most Merciful?' I said: 'Yes, by Him who sent Muhammad with the truth, it is truly His speech, which He revealed to His Prophet Muhammad.' He said to me: 'That is enough.' Then he went to the she-camel, slaughtered it and cut it all up, and said: 'Help me distribute it.' So we distributed it to those who came and went. Then he went to his sword and bow, broke them, placed them under the sand, and turned away fleeing toward the desert, saying: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised.﴾

I turned upon myself with blame and said: 'You did not take heed of what the Bedouin took heed of.' When I performed the pilgrimage with al-Rashid, I entered Mecca. While I was circling the Ka'bah, a caller called out to me with a thin voice. I turned, and there was the Bedouin, emaciated and yellowed, who greeted me, took my hand, and seated me behind the Maqam, and said to me: 'Recite the speech of the Most Merciful.' So I began the sura of al-Dhariyat, and when I reached His saying: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision, and what you are promised﴾, the Bedouin cried out and said: ﴿We have found what our Lord promised us to be true.﴾ Then he said: 'Is there anything other than this?' I said: 'Yes, Allah says: ﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth, [just] like what you speak.﴾' The Bedouin cried out and said: 'Glory be to Allah! Who is it that angered the Majestic until He swore? Did they not believe Him with His word, until they compelled Him to an oath?' He said it three times, and his soul departed upon it." [Kitab al-Tawwabin of Abd Allah ibn Qudamah: 275, no. 112.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Shayba narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim narrated to us, saying: Shabanah narrated to us, saying: Sadaqah narrated to us, saying: al-Wadin ibn Ata narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Jarir, that a man became hungry in a place where there was nothing. He said: "O Allah, grant me the provision You promised me, and bring it to me." He said: "So he was satisfied and quenched, without food or drink."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Khatib narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Muharrami narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Yazid al-Adnani narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Maysarah narrated to us, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If any one of you were to flee from his provision, it would pursue him just as death pursues him." [97] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/42.]

I also recited in its meaning:

"The provision is in nearness and in distance;
the servant seeks it from the servant.
If the seeker falls short in his striving,
what was decreed for him will still come to him in his intended goal."

Dabal said:

"I strive to seek my provision, while it seeks me;
the provision is more eager for me than I am for it."

[Rawdat al-Wa'izin: 5/426.]

﴿And in the earth are signs for those who are certain.﴾

﴿And in yourselves too. Will you not see?﴾

So he entered a ruin and remained there three days without obtaining anything. When it was the third day, he saw a cluster of dates (jullah min ratb). Mujahid said: ﴿and what you are promised﴾ is of good or evil. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿and what you are promised﴾ is of Paradise and Hell.

﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth, indeed it is the truth, [just] like what you speak.﴾ That is, that what you have mentioned concerning the matter of provision is true. [Grammatical analysis, i'rab, here concerns the case of the word.]

Al-Hasan said regarding this verse: "It has reached me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'May Allah fight against people to whom their Lord swore by Himself, yet they did not believe Him.'" [96] [Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 26/267.]

He drew near, greeted me, and said to me: 'Who is the man?' I said: 'From the Banu al-Asma'.' He said: 'Are you al-Asma'i?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And where have you come from?' Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 51, verse 24–45:

﴿Has there come to you, O Muhammad, the story of the honoured guests of Abraham?﴾ Scholars differ regarding their number. Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil said: they were twelve angels. Muhammad ibn Kaʿb said: Gabriel was with seven. ʿAta' and a group said: they were three: Gabriel, Michael, and another angel. ﴿The honoured ones.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: He called them "honoured" because they were not invited.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Sha'rani told me, saying:

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Saʿid al-Ar'yali informed us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Wahhab say: ʿAli ibn Ghannam said to me: "I have harisa (a dish of wheat and meat). What is your opinion of it?" I said: "What a fine opinion I have of it!" He said: "Go on." So I entered the house, and he began calling, "Boy! Boy!" while the boy was absent. He brought me into a room and I sat in it. Suddenly there was with him the ewer, the basin, and a towel over his shoulder. I said: "Indeed we belong to God, O Abu al-Hasan! Had I known the matter was like this with you, I would not have entered." He said: "Take it easy. Abu Usama related to us from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, glorified is He: ﴿Has there come to you the story of the honoured guests of Abraham?﴾ He said: 'His serving them with his own hands.'" ʿAbd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: "They were honoured with God. Its parallel is in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants.﴾"

Abu Bakr al-Warraq and Ibn ʿAta' said: He named them "honoured" because the guests of noble people are honoured, and Abraham, peace be upon him, was the most generous of creation and the most virtuous in chivalry.

﴿When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, people unknown."﴾ That is, "You are a people unknown, strangers whom we do not recognize." It was also said: he disapproved of their matter because they entered upon him without asking permission. Abu al-'Aliyah said: he disapproved of their greeting in that time and in that land.

﴿Then he turned away quietly to his family﴾: al-Farra' said: the word "rawagh" is not used unless its subject is hidden from the going and coming. ﴿And brought a fat calf﴾: Qatadah said: most of Abraham's wealth was cattle. ﴿And presented it to them, and said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ ﴿Then he felt apprehension of them. They said, "Do not fear." And they gave him good news of a knowledgeable boy.﴾ ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry⁠—﴾ that is, a shout. This was not coming from one place to another; rather it is like the saying of one who says, "He came at me cursing," meaning he began cursing me.

﴿And she struck her face﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: she slapped her face. Others said: she struck her palm on her forehead in amazement, as is the custom of women when they deny something or are astonished by it. The root of *sakk* is striking. ﴿And said, "An old, barren woman!"﴾ Its implied meaning: "Will an old barren woman give birth?" Sarah had not given birth before that, and between the good news and the birth was a year. Sarah gave birth to him when she was ninety-seven years old, and Abraham was one hundred years old.

﴿They said, "So (it will be). Your Lord has said, 'Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing.'"﴾ Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbduws narrated to us by dictation, saying:

Abu Sahl al-Qattan informed us in Baghdad, saying: Yahya ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun informed us; and Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf told us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Nasr ibn ʿAli told us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays informed us, saying: ʿAwn ibn Abi Shaddad told us that the guests of Abraham, the honoured ones, when they entered upon him and he brought near to them the calf, Gabriel, peace be upon him, swept it with his wing, and the calf got up, running in the house until it reached its mother.

﴿He said, "What is your business, O messengers?" They said, "Indeed we have been sent to a criminal people, to send upon them stones of clay,﴾ al-Kalbi said: "of baked clay (sink)," and its explanation is His words: ﴿of sijjil﴾ ﴿marked by your Lord for the transgressors.﴾ ﴿So We brought out whoever was there of the believers. But We found not there except one house of Muslims.﴾

﴿And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.﴾

﴿And in Moses⁠—﴾ that is, and We left a sign also in the sending of Moses. Al-Farra' said: it is conjoined with His words: ﴿And in the earth are signs...﴾ ﴿And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority.﴾ ﴿But he turned away with his supporters﴾: he turned away and withdrew from faith, relying on his strength and his people. Its parallel is ﴿or I would take refuge in a strong support﴾, meaning power and kin. Al-Mu'arrikh said: "with his side." ﴿And said, "A magician or a madman."﴾ Abu ʿUbaydah said: "aw" here means "wa" (and), since they said both together. He recited the verse of Jarir:

*"Ath'alabatu al-fawaris aw Riyahan... 'adalat bihim Tuhayyatu wal-Khashabah"* [Lisan al-'Arab: 15/17.]

And "aw" may be used to mean "wa," as in His words: ﴿sinful or ungrateful﴾; and "wa" may mean "aw," as in His words, glorified is He: ﴿Marry what seems good to you of women, two or three or four﴾.

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, and he was blameworthy.﴾ He had done what deserved blame.

﴿And in ʿAd, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which does not fertilize trees, does not produce clouds, and has no mercy or blessing in it, ﴿that left nothing it came upon but made it like the rotted.﴾ Like a plant that has dried and been trampled.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: like a thing destroyed. Muqatil: like something decayed. Mujahid: like dry straw. Qatadah: like crumbled tree wood. Abu al-'Aliyah: like crushed dust. Yaman said: what cattle scatter with their dung from the fodder; and it is said of the crushed remains: *al-marmah* and *al-maqmah*. It was also said: its origin is from decayed bone.

﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time."﴾ That is, until the time of the end of their lifespans.

﴿But they defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.﴾ Al-Husayn ibn Waqid said: every "sa'iqah" (thunderbolt) in the Qur'an is a punishment. Looking at it by day.

﴿Then they were not able to rise up, nor were they able to defend themselves.﴾ That is, they did not rise after the punishment descended upon them, nor were they able to stand up to it or defend against it. ﴿And they were not among those who could help themselves⁠—﴾ avenging themselves against Us.

Qatadah said: they had no strength by which they could protect themselves from God.

He brought me into a room and I sat in it. Suddenly there was with him the ewer, the basin, and a towel over his shoulder. I said: "Indeed we belong to God, O Abu al-Hasan! Had I known the matter was like this with you, I would not have entered." He said: "Take it easy. Abu Usama related to us from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, glorified is He: ﴿Has there come to you the story of the honoured guests of Abraham?﴾ He said: 'His serving them with his own hands.'" ʿAbd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Kinani said: "They were honoured with God. Its parallel is in Surat al-Anbiya': ﴿Rather, they are honoured servants.﴾"

Abu Bakr al-Warraq and Ibn ʿAta' said: He named them "honoured" because the guests of noble people are honoured, and Abraham, peace be upon him, was the most generous of creation and the most virtuous in chivalry.

﴿When they entered upon him and said, "Peace." He said, "Peace, people unknown."﴾ That is, "You are a people unknown, strangers whom we do not recognize." It was also said: he disapproved of their matter because they entered upon him without asking permission. Abu al-'Aliyah said: he disapproved of their greeting in that time and in that land.

﴿Then he turned away quietly to his family﴾: al-Farra' said: the word "rawagh" is not used unless its subject is hidden from the going and coming. ﴿And brought a fat calf﴾: Qatadah said: most of Abraham's wealth was cattle. ﴿And presented it to them, and said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ ﴿Then he felt apprehension of them. They said, "Do not fear." And they gave him good news of a knowledgeable boy.﴾ ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry⁠—﴾ that is, a shout. This was not coming from one place to another; rather it is like the saying of one who says, "He came at me cursing," meaning he began cursing me.

﴿And she struck her face﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: she slapped her face. Others said: she struck her palm on her forehead in amazement, as is the custom of women when they deny something or are astonished by it. The root of *sakk* is striking. ﴿And said, "An old, barren woman!"﴾ Its implied meaning: "Will an old barren woman give birth?" Sarah had not given birth before that, and between the good news and the birth was a year. Sarah gave birth to him when she was ninety-seven years old, and Abraham was one hundred years old.

﴿They said, "So (it will be). Your Lord has said, 'Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing.'"﴾ Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbduws narrated to us by dictation, saying:

Abu Sahl al-Qattan informed us in Baghdad, saying: Yahya ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun informed us; and Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf told us, saying: Yusuf ibn Ya'qub told us, saying: Nasr ibn ʿAli told us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays informed us, saying: ʿAwn ibn Abi Shaddad told us that the guests of Abraham, the honoured ones, when they entered upon him and he brought near to them the calf, Gabriel, peace be upon him, swept it with his wing, and the calf got up, running in the house until it reached its mother.

﴿He said, "What is your business, O messengers?" They said, "Indeed we have been sent to a criminal people, to send upon them stones of clay,﴾ al-Kalbi said: "of baked clay (sink)," and its explanation is His words: ﴿of sijjil﴾ ﴿marked by your Lord for the transgressors.﴾ ﴿So We brought out whoever was there of the believers. But We found not there except one house of Muslims.﴾

﴿And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.﴾

﴿And in Moses⁠—﴾ that is, and We left a sign also in the sending of Moses. Al-Farra' said: it is conjoined with His words: ﴿And in the earth are signs...﴾ ﴿And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority.﴾ ﴿But he turned away with his supporters﴾: he turned away and withdrew from faith, relying on his strength and his people. Its parallel is ﴿or I would take refuge in a strong support﴾, meaning power and kin. Al-Mu'arrikh said: "with his side." ﴿And said, "A magician or a madman."﴾ Abu ʿUbaydah said: "aw" here means "wa" (and), since they said both together. He recited the verse of Jarir:

*"Ath'alabatu al-fawaris aw Riyahan... 'adalat bihim Tuhayyatu wal-Khashabah"* [Lisan al-'Arab: 15/17.]

And "aw" may be used to mean "wa," as in His words: ﴿sinful or ungrateful﴾; and "wa" may mean "aw," as in His words, glorified is He: ﴿Marry what seems good to you of women, two or three or four﴾.

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea, and he was blameworthy.﴾ He had done what deserved blame.

﴿And in ʿAd, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾, which does not fertilize trees, does not produce clouds, and has no mercy or blessing in it, ﴿that left nothing it came upon but made it like the rotted.﴾ Like a plant that has dried and been trampled.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: like a thing destroyed. Muqatil: like something decayed. Mujahid: like dry straw. Qatadah: like crumbled tree wood. Abu al-'Aliyah: like crushed dust. Yaman said: what cattle scatter with their dung from the fodder; and it is said of the crushed remains: *al-marmah* and *al-maqmah*. It was also said: its origin is from decayed bone.

﴿And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time."﴾ That is, until the time of the end of their lifespans.

﴿But they defied the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on.﴾ Al-Husayn ibn Waqid said: every "sa'iqah" (thunderbolt) in the Qur'an is a punishment. Looking at it by day.

﴿Then they were not able to rise up, nor were they able to defend themselves.﴾ That is, they did not rise after the punishment descended upon them, nor were they able to stand up to it or defend against it. ﴿And they were not among those who could help themselves⁠—﴾ avenging themselves against Us.

Qatadah said: they had no strength by which they could protect themselves from God.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 51, verse 46–60:

﴿وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ﴾ Abu 'Amr, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read (wa-qawmi) with a kasra on the mim in qawmi nuhin, while the rest read it with a fatha. It has several possible readings. One: it is governed by the pronoun (hum) and (mim) in His words ﴿فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ﴾, meaning "and the thunderbolt seized the people of Nuh." The second: "And We destroyed the people of Nuh." The third:

"And remember the people of Nuh before them," meaning before 'Ad, Thamud and the people of Pharaoh. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا قَوْماً فاسِقِينَ﴾ — "Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people."

﴿وَالسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأَيْدٍ﴾ — "And the sky We constructed with power," ﴿وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ﴾ — "and indeed We are its expander." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Capable." He also said: "Expanding provision for Our creation." al-Dahhak said: "Wealthy." Its proof is His words ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ﴾. al-Qutaybi said: "Possessors of abundance over Our creation." al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "Our knowledge encompasses everything." al-Hasan said: "Those who extend (the heavens)."

﴿وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْناها﴾ — "And the earth, We spread it out," meaning We extended and smoothed it for you, ﴿فَنِعْمَ الْماهِدُونَ﴾ — "and how excellent are the ones who spread out." The plural here conveys magnification.

﴿وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾ — "And of everything We created pairs," meaning two kinds and two different types, such as the sky and the earth, the sun and the moon, the night and the day, the land and the sea, the plain and the mountain, winter and summer, the jinn and mankind, disbelief and faith, wretchedness and happiness, truth and falsehood, male and female, Paradise and Hellfire.

﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ — "So that you may remember," that is, so that you may know that the Creator of pairs is One.

﴿فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ — "So flee to Allah," that is: flee from the punishment of Allah to His reward, through faith and abstaining from disobedience.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Flee from Him to Him, and act in obedience to Him." Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "Flee from obedience to Satan to obedience to the Merciful." Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hamdan ibn Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar narrated to us from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, concerning His words ﴿فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾, that he said: "Go out to Makkah." al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "Guard yourselves against everything other than Him, for whoever flees to other than Him will not be protected from Him."

al-Junayd said: "Satan is a caller to falsehood; ﴿فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ — He will protect you from him." Dhu al-Nun said: "Flee from ignorance to knowledge, and from disbelief to gratitude." 'Amr ibn 'Uthman said: "Flee from yourselves to your Lord." al-Wasiti said: "Flee to what has preceded for you from Allah, and do not rely on your own movements." Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Flee from what is other than Allah to Allah." ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ — "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him."

﴿وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ — "And do not make with Allah another god. Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him." ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ — that is: just as your people denied you and said, "a sorcerer" and "a madman," ﴿ما أَتَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا قالُوا ساحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ﴾ — "Thus no messenger came to those before them except that they said, 'A sorcerer or a madman.'"

﴿أَتَواصَوْا بِهِ﴾ — "Did they enjoin it upon one another?" meaning: did they recommend to one another the denial and conspire together upon it? The alif in it is the alif of reproach.

﴿بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ﴾ — "Rather, they are a people who transgress," meaning rebellious and disobedient.

﴿فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَما أَنْتَ بِمَلُومٍ﴾ — "So turn away from them, and you are not to be blamed," for you have conveyed what you were sent with, and you did not fall short in what you were commanded.

The exegetes said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, and that weighed heavily upon his companions, and they thought that revelation had ceased and that punishment had drawn near. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿ذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرى تَنْفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ * وَما خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنْسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾

'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: its meaning is "except that I command them to worship Me, and I call them to My worship." al-Zajjaj adopted this view, and it is supported by His words ﴿وَما أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا إِلهاً واحِداً﴾ and His words ﴿وَما أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "That they may acknowledge My lordship willingly or unwillingly."

If it is asked: how did they disbelieve when He created them to acknowledge His lordship and to submit humbly to His command and His will, and they have submitted humbly to His decree which He decreed upon them?

[We say:] Because His decree is carried out upon them, and they cannot resist it when it descends upon them; what opposes Him is only the one who disbelieves in Him in acting upon what He commanded. As for submission to His decree, there is no refusal in it. Mujahid said: "except that they may know Me" (ليعرفون).

This view is excellent, because if He had not created them, He would not have been known, nor His oneness. Its proof is His words ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ (the verses).

Hayyan narrated from al-Kalbi: "except that they may affirm My oneness." As for the believer, he affirms His oneness in hardship and ease; as for the disbeliever, he affirms His oneness in hardship and calamity but not in blessing and ease. Its clarification is His words: ﴿فَإِذا رَكِبُوا فِي الْفُلْكِ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ (the verse).

'Ikrimah said: ﴿إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾ "and obey." Thus the worshipper is rewarded and the denier is punished. al-Dahhak and Sufyan said: this is specific to the people of His worship and obedience. It is indicated by what Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿وَما خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنْسَ﴾ "from among the believers" ﴿إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾. He said in another verse: ﴿وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيراً مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ﴾. Some of them said: the meaning is "I created the blessed among the jinn and mankind only for My worship, and the wretched among them only for My disobedience." This is the meaning of the saying of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "What they were molded upon of wretchedness and happiness." al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the apparent servitude.

But this is not the sense, because if He had power over them to make them worship Him, they would not have disobeyed Him nor worshipped other than Him. It is rather like His words: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾, then He said: ﴿قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ and ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾.

The general meaning of the verse is that Allah, exalted is He, did not create them for worship by natural disposition and compulsion, but created them for it by way of obligation and choice. Whoever He grants success and guidance establishes the worship for which he was created, and whoever He forsakes and drives away is deprived of it and acts by what he was created for.

As in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for."

[98] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/82.]] And Allah knows best.

﴿ما أُرِيدُ مِنْهُمْ مِنْ رِزْقٍ﴾ — "I do not want from them any provision," that is, provision, ﴿وَما أُرِيدُ أَنْ يُطْعِمُونِ﴾ — "and I do not want them to feed Me." ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ﴾ — "Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm." The common reading is with a damma on the nun, as a description of Allah, glorified and exalted is He: the Strong, the Capable, the one greatly mighty in strength and power.

Ibn 'Abbas said: al-matin is the hard and firm. Yahya and al-A'mash read al-matini with a kasra, as an adjective of al-quwwa. al-Farra' said: its original form should have been feminine, but it was made masculine because it refers to a thing that is firmly twisted and tightly wound, as one says "a firm rope" (habl matin). al-Farra' recited:

"For every age you have worn garments, until the head was covered with a white veil,
of the fine ribbon and the striped Yemeni cloth."

He made "al-mu'assab" masculine because "al-yamanah" is a kind of garment.

From this category is His words: ﴿فَمَنْ جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ﴾ — meaning admonition, and His words ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ — meaning the cry and the sound.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us, saying: al-Qutayfi narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Adam and Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, both saying: Isra'il narrated to us from Abu Ishaq from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught me: "Indeed I am the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm."

﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ — "So that you may remember," that is, so that you may know that the Creator of pairs is One.

﴿فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ — "So flee to Allah," that is: flee from the punishment of Allah to His reward, through faith and abstaining from disobedience.

﴿بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طاغُونَ﴾ — "Rather, they are a people who transgress," meaning rebellious and disobedient.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "That they may acknowledge My lordship willingly or unwillingly."

Some of them said: the meaning is "I created the blessed among the jinn and mankind only for My worship, and the wretched among them only for My disobedience." This is the meaning of the saying of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "What they were molded upon of wretchedness and happiness." al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the apparent servitude.

But this is not the sense, because if He had power over them to make them worship Him, they would not have disobeyed Him nor worshipped other than Him. It is rather like His words: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾, then He said: ﴿قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ and ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾.

The general meaning of the verse is that Allah, exalted is He, did not create them for worship by natural disposition and compulsion, but created them for it by way of obligation and choice. Whoever He grants success and guidance establishes the worship for which he was created, and whoever He forsakes and drives away is deprived of it and acts by what he was created for.

As in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for."

"For every age you have worn garments, until the head was covered with a white veil,
of the fine ribbon and the striped Yemeni cloth."

﴿فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ — "So flee to Allah," that is: flee from the punishment of Allah to His reward, through faith and abstaining from disobedience.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Flee from Him to Him, and act in obedience to Him." Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "Flee from obedience to Satan to obedience to the Merciful." Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: "Flee from what is other than Allah to Allah." ﴿إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ — "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him."

﴿وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ — "And do not make with Allah another god. [We say:] Because His decree is carried out upon them, and they cannot resist it when it descends upon them; what opposes Him is only the one who disbelieves in Him in acting upon what He commanded. The common reading is with a damma on the nun, as a description of Allah, glorified and exalted is He: the Strong, the Capable, the one greatly mighty in strength and power.

Ibn 'Abbas said: al-matin is the hard and firm. "For every age you have worn garments, until the head was covered with a white veil,
of the fine ribbon and the striped Yemeni cloth."

He made "al-mu'assab" masculine because "al-yamanah" is a kind of garment.

From this category is His words: ﴿فَمَنْ جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ﴾ — meaning admonition, and His words ﴿وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ — meaning the cry and the sound.

The original meaning of dhanub in the language is a large, great bucket full of water.

The reciter said:
"For them a bucket, and for you a bucket;
if you refuse, then for us is the well."

Then it is used for portion and share, as in the saying of 'Alqamah ibn 'Abidah:

It is indicated by what Ibn 'Abbas recited: ﴿وَما خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنْسَ﴾ "from among the believers" ﴿إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ﴾. Some of them said: the meaning is "I created the blessed among the jinn and mankind only for My worship, and the wretched among them only for My disobedience." This is the meaning of the saying of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: "What they were molded upon of wretchedness and happiness." al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the apparent servitude.

But this is not the sense, because if He had power over them to make them worship Him, they would not have disobeyed Him nor worshipped other than Him. It is rather like His words: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾, then He said: ﴿قَلِيلًا ما تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ and ﴿وَقَلِيلٌ مِنْ عِبادِيَ الشَّكُورُ﴾.
